name: Otto von Bismarck
role: Minister President of Prussia (1862-1890) and first Chancellor of the German Empire (1871-1890)
summary: Prussian conservative statesman who unified Germany under the Prussian crown through the wars of 1864-71, ruled through the monarch with a weakened Reichstag, and fought political Catholicism and Social Democracy. He also created state sickness, accident and old-age insurance and moved from free trade to protective tariffs, while avoiding European war after 1871.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sponsored the 1883 compulsory sickness insurance for industrial workers (employer and worker contributions, sick pay and medical treatment), but it covered only part of the population and was not tax-funded universal care.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: he rejected free-trade doctrine for protective tariffs, proposed a tobacco monopoly and state insurance, yet said he was not hostile to capital and welcomed wealthy classes; he judged by experience, not market theory.

public-ownership.rationale: Said in the Reichstag in 1878 that he aimed at a state tobacco monopoly and held the state a better and more conscientious trader than the private entrepreneur; the monopoly bill of 1882 failed.

unions-good.rationale: Mixed: the 1869 trade code legalised workers' coalitions under the North German Confederation he led, but the 1878 Anti-Socialist Law he proposed dissolved social-democratic associations including their unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: In 1884 he defended the Stein-Hardenberg reforms as justified state socialism, in which the law took part of an owner's land for the tenant, and said the state may cut with the surgeon's knife where privilege forms a chain; he also protected landowners' interests.

cut-welfare.rationale: Told the Reichstag in 1884 that the state has a duty to care for helpless citizens, rejected leaving it to private companies, and created sickness, accident and old-age insurance.

worker-ownership.rationale: In 1865 he persuaded the king to advance royal funds to Silesian weavers for a co-operative factory as a test of productive associations and said he had talked with Lassalle about co-operative production; he never legislated it.

strong-leader.rationale: Argued that parliament can veto and check but cannot rule, governed through the 1862-66 budget conflict without an approved budget, and ruled through the monarch; yet said he in no way supported an absolutist government.

state-harmful.rationale: Held that the state, by its nature, has duties such as defence, transport and care of the needy, and that the Reich must act; the idea of an unnecessary state is incompatible with his stated views.

empower-police-military.rationale: Asked the Reichstag in 1888 to make Germany as strong as possible militarily, defended Prussian army reform against the liberals in 1862, and drove the Anti-Socialist Law that expanded police powers.

more-religion-public.rationale: Said in 1847 that a state must stand on a religious foundation and in 1881-82 called his social policy practical Christianity, yet in 1882 said whether the state is formally Christian was beside the point, and he fought the Church politically.

gradual-change.rationale: Wrote that great nations are ponderous masses that can only move with caution, and that losing the restraining influence of the propertied class leads to a speed that shatters the coach of state, as in the French Revolution.

free-trade.rationale: Broke with free trade in 1879: told the Reichstag that protected countries prosper and open ones decline, and enacted industrial and agricultural tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: Told the Reichstag in 1881 that his compass was salus publica, with his first thought for the nation, its position abroad and its independence; his Realpolitik put German interests first.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mixed: opposed revolution at home (1848, social democracy), but wrote that in a fight against an overwhelming foreign power he did not hesitate to use even revolutionary means, such as universal suffrage in 1866.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Enacted the 1879 protective tariffs on industry and agriculture and argued in the Reichstag in May 1879 that protected countries prosper and that protection was Prussia's traditional policy.

one-party-rule.rationale: Said in 1881 that he had never been doctrinaire and that the systems dividing parties were of secondary moment to him; he governed with shifting coalitions.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Wrote that he had grown up in royalist traditions and needed a monarchical institution for his earthly well-being, and was until death the king's faithful subject.

democracy-best.rationale: Wrote that a state controlled by the greedy and by orators able to deceive the masses is doomed to restlessness, and wanted propertied influence to outweigh mass voting; he held parliament should veto but not rule.

separate-church-state.rationale: Held that a state should stand on a religious foundation (1847) and that Protestant Kaiserdom and Rome would always conflict; the Kulturkampf subordinated the church to the state rather than separating them.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Listed national defence and justice-related duties among tasks only the state can fulfil, and said these could not be left to private stock companies.

military-superiority.rationale: Told the Reichstag in 1888 that Germany must be as strong as it possibly can, strong enough to face any coalition, and asked for the army bill.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Dawson summarises his view that social duties are imposed on citizens and the state ensures they are discharged; he did not frame it against individual rights.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said in 1881 that he had never been doctrinaire, and in 1879 that he judged by experience and not scientific doctrine; Dawson records his dictum that an ounce of fact outweighs a ton of theory.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: said in 1882 he was not antagonistic to the rightful claims of capital and that a landowner has a right to rent and a capitalist to profit.

conscription.rationale: Sought the 1888 army bill to extend military service obligations to make the nation's strength fully available, and defended the Prussian conscription army since 1862.

positive-liberty.rationale: Told the Reichstag in 1884 that no one has a use for the freedom to starve and that freedom is a vague term often meaning domination, justifying compulsory insurance.

organic-representation.rationale: Created the Prussian Economic Council in 1881, with members nominated by trade, industry and agriculture, as an advisory body; he kept the elected Reichstag and the Bundesrat.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Mixed: annexed Schleswig, Hanover and Alsace-Lorraine in the 1860s-70s, but from 1871 treated Germany as satisfied; in 1888 said he would not kindle a war, and he resisted colonies until 1884.

national-self-determination.rationale: Mixed: pursued German national unity in a Prussian-led state, but denied Polish, Danish and Alsatian claims to their own states.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Told the Reichstag in 1882 that his belief in the moral law of revealed religion was sufficient for him and that, as a Christian, he acted so as to be justified before God.

class-collaboration.rationale: As reported by Dawson, held that classes rest on mutual obligation, mutual dependence and help, and that the state must intervene for conciliation; he preached the rich's duty to neighbours.

workers-nation.rationale: Said in 1884 that Social Democracy's goals could not be realised in one state and would need an international basis that would never exist; his answer to workers was national state insurance.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rejected in 1884 the idea that the state is limited to security, saying it has duties for the poor and sick and that every poor law is socialism, and enacted state insurance.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Accepted the 1874-75 compulsory civil marriage law for all Prussians, saying marriage is a municipal matter in Luther's view, although he said his acceptance rested on yielding to ministers.

population-transfer.rationale: As Prussian minister-president he defended the 1885 expulsion of about 48,000 Poles and Polish Jews lacking citizenship, and said those hostile to the state should withdraw from it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Said politics is made by blood and iron, not majority resolutions, and led Prussia into wars in 1864, 1866 and 1870.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Said in 1888 that France and Russia act like pikes in a carp-pond, spurring Germans to exertion and unity they would not otherwise achieve.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Proposed and drove the 1878 Anti-Socialist Law banning Social Democratic associations, and said in 1886 that those who negate the state have no rights in it.

separated-powers.rationale: Said in 1884 that parliament should be able to veto bad laws and curb waste but not rule; the 1867 constitution divided power between the Bundesrat, Reichstag and the presidency.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Told the Prussian Diet in 1865 that the kings of Prussia were never kings of the rich but protectors of the poor, and in 1884 stressed the benefit to the poor and needy in state insurance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The 1878 Anti-Socialist Law he proposed allowed, in districts where public safety was threatened, banning meetings and expelling persons from localities for up to a year.

head-commands-forces.rationale: In his 1866 Putbus dictations he assigned war and peace, mobilisation and supreme command to the king as commander-in-chief and Bundesfeldherr of the new confederation.

clerical-rule.rationale: Said priests are sworn officers in the army of a non-Prussian sovereign and wanted the state to weaken their hold on lay Catholics; he fought political Catholicism in the Kulturkampf.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Built the Dual Alliance (1879), League of Three Emperors, Triple Alliance (1882) and Reinsurance Treaty (1887), and in 1888 stressed confidence in Germany's treaties.

people-in-arms.rationale: Defended the standing army against liberal budget cuts in 1862, telling the budget committee the government must reject views that all standing armies are superfluous.

minority-language-support.rationale: Led a policy of Germanisation toward Poles, Danes and French speakers, and in 1886 said Polish-speaking provinces needed a change from the post-1840 approach.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Defended the Stein-Hardenberg land transfer and the state's right to cut away privilege where law and privilege form a coercive chain, as state socialism.

collective-defense.rationale: Concluded the Dual Alliance (1879) and Triple Alliance (1882), pledging mutual assistance against attack by Russia and others.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Took Alsace-Lorraine from France in 1871 without a plebiscite and annexed Hanover and Schleswig; he treated them as lawful acquisitions by treaty.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Pushed the Kulturkampf: dissolved the Catholic department of the Prussian ministry, demanded the constitutional changes behind the May Laws and wanted lay education to weaken priestly influence.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Claimed in 1862-66 the right to govern without a budget but sought parliament's retroactive indemnity in 1866, spoke of a community based on law rather than force in 1867, and denied supporting absolutism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Refused Polish self-governing institutions, calling Polish national aims hostile to the Prussian state and defending a Germanisation policy.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: from his stated need for the monarchical institution and royalist traditions; he spoke of kings inheriting.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Told the Reichstag in 1884 that parliament can prevent evil and bad laws but cannot rule; ruled through the Crown and the Bundesrat, with the Reichstag sidelined.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Praised, in 1885, large landowners who live on their estates and are mindful of their duties, and Dawson records that he preached the rich's duty to neighbours and enforced it through the state.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Told the Reichstag in 1884 that leaving insurance to private companies charging premiums at market rates would abandon a state duty; he built state-run old-age and invalidity insurance.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Mixed: in 1862-66 governed without an approved budget under the gap theory; in 1866 asked parliament to indemnify retroactively and in 1884 said parliament should hinder the squandering of money.

single-official-language.rationale: Pursued a policy of Germanisation toward Polish, Danish and French-speaking minorities, with German as the language of administration and schooling.

job-guarantee.rationale: Told the Reichstag in May 1884, as reported by Dawson, that he unconditionally acknowledged a right to work and that the state should undertake public works for the unemployed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Contested: claimed in 1886 that Polish nobles and the Polish clergy aimed to detach Prussian territory and would take arms against Prussia, and said the Catholic department Polonised the administration.

religion-illusion.rationale: Said in 1882 that his belief in revealed religion as moral law was enough for him and that he acted as a Christian before God.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mixed: banned Social Democratic organisations and said those who negate the state have no rights in it, but in 1884 denied that he treated any opposition as reprehensible and allowed parliamentary opposition.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: In 1862 told the king that his rights were assigned to him by the grace of God, and said that a state must rest on a religious foundation; he also accepted a popularly elected Reichstag.

social-market-economy.rationale: Combined private capital, which he welcomed, with state social insurance and tariffs; he did not state fair-competition rules as a goal.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Argued as chancellor that Germany must be armed to withstand any coalition and sought the 1888 military bill.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Joined the Dual Alliance and the Triple Alliance and maintained links with Russia, rather than staying out of great-power blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: from his support for hereditary monarchy and its royalist traditions, which include succession within the dynasty.

property-franchise.rationale: Wrote that universal suffrage is just in principle if open, but that a preponderance of property-holders serves the state better; in 1866 floated a plan where half the Reichstag was chosen by the highest taxpayers, yet the 1867 Reichstag franchise was universal male.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said in the Reichstag that he wished a few hundred millionaires might be created because their spending benefits labour; this contradicts the claim, though he never discussed liberty and wealth.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: he held the state should stand on a religious foundation and spoke of practical Christianity, which excludes an atheist state.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Told the Reichstag in 1884 that the state could not leave care of the helpless to private stock companies and that the state must care for the poor and old.

second-chamber.rationale: Mixed: designed the Bundesrat as a federal body that passed laws with the Reichstag, but rejected a bicameral Reichstag and said the Bundesrat was not an upper house.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Mixed: opposed preventive wars (Luxembourg 1867, 1875) and in 1888 said he would not kindle a war, but initiated the wars of 1864 and 1866.

arms-reduction.rationale: Argued in 1888 that Germany's geographic position required larger military exertions than any other nation, and sought the army bill.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Concluded the 1887 Reinsurance Treaty with Russia with a strictly secret protocol not revealed until the First World War, as well as secret alliance engagements.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: from his insistence on army obedience in the 1862-67 conflict and military strength.

notes: Several positions changed over time: free trader until 1876 then protectionist from 1878-79; ally of the National Liberals and Kulturkampf until 1878-79, then allied with the Centre and conservatives; opposed colonies until 1884. Answers on social insurance rely on his 1884 speech and Dawson's quotations of 1881-85 speeches. Memoir passages are his dictated words. Jewish emancipation (1869), the 1881 Imperial Message and railway nationalisation were not read in full text and are left null.
